seo.Meta description: Book LEO Section tickets at Rajadamnern Stadium. Section 10, front-facing view, seat guaranteed.

Intro: The LEO Section is Section 10, the main-arena seating that faces the front of the ring. It sits at exactly the same elevation as Club Class, with the same number of rows, and it is where the camera gantry, the commentary team, the local Muay Thai crowd and the loudest reactions in the stadium all sit together.
Every LEO ticket guarantees a seat. You pick your position within the section when you arrive, and you can move during the night if a better spot opens up.
Fact strip: View: Front-facing, same elevation as Club Class

H2: Why guests book LEO Section Rajadamnern Stadium tickets
Tile 1: The camera gantry and commentary team are in LEO. Sports cameras go where the whole fight can be seen.
Tile 2: Exactly the same elevation and number of rows. The difference is that LEO faces the front of the ring.
Tile 3: Pick your position within Section 10 when you arrive. Front row is yours if it is free when you walk in. Every ticket guarantees a seat.
Tile 4: Servers work inside the section all night. Beer and food come to you. On RWS Saturdays the beer is included.

H2: Book LEO Section tickets at Rajadamnern Stadium
Urgency line: LEO sells out first on Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday, and about a week ahead for RWS Saturdays. MuayTix often holds tickets after the stadium has sold out.
Intro: Select your date, confirm LEO and complete your booking securely online. You receive a booking confirmation straight away, and your seat in Section 10 is guaranteed.
Trust line: Your payment details are encrypted and protected by Stripe's enterprise-level security.

H2: The view from Section 10 Rajadamnern Stadium
Headline: Face the ring, not the side of it.
Body: LEO looks straight at the front of the ring. Club Class, next door, looks towards the sides. You share the same elevation and the same rows, so the difference is direction, not height.

That direction matters more than most first-time visitors expect. The blue corner is directly in front of the section, the fighters enter past it, and the commentary team sits here. The camera gantry is in LEO, so the main broadcast cameras shoot from this side because it gives the clearest read of the whole canvas. When the referee raises the winner's hand at the end of a bout, the fighters are facing LEO.
Detail: MuayTix recommends around Row D and above for the fullest elevated view across the ring. Front row gives a flatter, closer, almost eye-level view. Both are good seats. The choice is yours on the night.

H2: LEO Section Muay Thai atmosphere at Rajadamnern
Headline: Sit with the people who follow this sport every week.
Body: LEO is the section local Muay Thai fans choose. It is louder, more communal and more reactive than anywhere else in the stadium, and it is where the MuayTix team sits when we come to watch for ourselves.

On the traditional Muay Thai nights, Wednesday New Power, Thursday Petchyindee and Sunday Kiatpetch, the local legal betting crowd gathers in Section 10. Odds move by hand signal, the noise rises and falls with every exchange, and you feel the fight through the crowd as much as you see it in the ring. You sit alongside it without taking part.
Detail: That betting atmosphere belongs to those three nights. Saturday RWS and the other events bring a different crowd, but LEO stays the most energetic section in the building.

H2: Is LEO Section unassigned seating? Yes, with a seat guaranteed
Headline: Unassigned means you choose. It never means you stand.
Body: LEO is concrete bench seating in Section 10, with 300 seats and strict control of ticket numbers. Every ticket has a seat waiting. There is no standing area and no risk of arriving to find the section full.

Unassigned seating gives you control after you walk in. You do not need to study a seat map or guess which row will suit you. Doors open one hour before the first bout. Arrive at opening if you want the full choice of rows, including front row. Arrive later if you are not fussed about the exact row, because your seat is still there.
Detail: If a better position opens up during the night, you can move to it. For groups, that flexibility is the reason LEO works so well: you sit together wherever you like.

H2: Food and drink service in the LEO Section
Headline: Order from your seat. On RWS Saturdays, the beer is included.
Body: Servers operate inside LEO throughout the event. Beer and food are brought to you, paid for separately as you order, so you never miss a round queuing at a bar.
On every Saturday RWS Rajadamnern World Series event, free-flow beer is included with your LEO ticket at the normal 1,500 THB price.
Detail: Free-flow beer applies to Saturday RWS only. On all other nights, LEO service is pay as you order.

H2: LEO Section availability and when to book
Headline: LEO sells out first. Book before the stadium does.
Body: On Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday traditional nights, LEO is the first public section to sell out, ahead of Ringside and Club Class, and it can be gone a day or two before the fight. For Saturday RWS, LEO commonly sells out around a week in advance.
MuayTix pre-buys LEO stock, so we often still hold tickets after the stadium has sold out. On 30 September the stadium had no LEO left for New Power while MuayTix still had tickets available.
Detail: If you want LEO for an RWS Saturday or a traditional night, book as early as you can. Live availability is shown in the booking widget above.

H2: Who should choose the LEO Section?
Tile 1: You want to feel the crowd as well as watch the fight
Especially on Wednesday, Thursday or Sunday, when the local crowd fills Section 10.
Tile 2: You want the front-facing view of the ring
The same elevation as Club Class, looking straight at the action.
Tile 3: You like to pick your own position
Front row, Row D, the back row. Decide when you see the ring.
Tile 4: You are coming as a group
Sit together wherever you like, with servers bringing drinks to the section.
Tile 5: You are going to Saturday RWS
Free-flow beer included at the normal LEO price.

H2: LEO Section or another Rajadamnern Stadium seat class?
Body: Choose LEO for the front-facing view, the freedom to pick your position, service to your seat and the strongest atmosphere in the stadium.
Choose Club Class for the same elevation with an assigned, numbered seat.
Choose Ringside to sit a few metres from the ring on the arena floor.
Choose Third Class for the widest view across the whole stadium from the highest tier, on the nights it opens.

faq.q: What is the LEO Section at Rajadamnern Stadium?
faq.a: The Rajadamnern LEO Section is Section 10, main-arena seating that faces the front of the ring at exactly the same elevation as Club Class. It has 300 unassigned seats, in-section food and drink service, and the strongest local atmosphere in the stadium. Tickets are 1,500 THB.

faq.q: Is LEO Section the same as Section 10?
faq.a: Yes. LEO Section and Section 10 are the same section. Rajadamnern Stadium numbers its sections, and LEO is the name used for Section 10.

faq.q: Was the LEO Section called Second Class?
faq.a: Yes. Older guides and some ticket listings call Section 10 Second Class, 2nd Class, LEO Second Class or LEO Class. They all mean the same section. LEO Section is the current name.
No. LEO is unassigned seating. You pick your position within Section 10 when you arrive, and you can move to another free position during the event.

faq.q: Do I have to stand in LEO?
faq.a: No. Every LEO ticket guarantees a seat. LEO is concrete bench seating with strict control of ticket numbers, and there is no standing area.

faq.q: Do I need to arrive early to get a seat in LEO?
faq.a: No. Your seat is guaranteed whenever you arrive. Arriving when doors open, one hour before the first bout, gives you the widest choice of position, including front row.

faq.q: Is LEO the same level as Club Class?
faq.a: Yes. LEO has exactly the same elevation and the same number of rows as Club Class. LEO faces the front of the ring, while Club Class looks towards the sides.

faq.q: What view do you get from LEO?
faq.a: A front-facing view across the whole ring from an elevated position, with the blue corner directly in front of the section. The camera gantry and commentary team are positioned in LEO.

faq.q: Which rows are best in LEO?
faq.a: MuayTix recommends around Row D and above for the fullest elevated view. Front row gives a closer, almost eye-level view of the ring. Both are good positions.

On Wednesday New Power, Thursday Petchyindee and Sunday Kiatpetch, the local legal betting crowd gathers in LEO and creates a high-energy atmosphere. On other nights LEO is simply the section local Muay Thai fans prefer.

faq.q: Do I have to take part in betting?
faq.a: No. You sit alongside the atmosphere and watch the fight. Nobody expects you to take part.

faq.q: Is free-flow beer included in LEO?
faq.a: Only on Saturday RWS Rajadamnern World Series events, when free-flow beer is included with the LEO ticket at the normal 1,500 THB price. On other nights, servers bring drinks to the section and you pay as you order.

faq.q: Is LEO suitable for children and families?
faq.a: Yes. There is no age restriction, and the open bench seating lets families and groups sit together wherever they like.

H2: Book the LEO Section at Rajadamnern Stadium
Body: Front-facing view, seat guaranteed, service to your section and the atmosphere the stadium is known for. Section 10 sells out first on the big nights, so book your date now.
